references.query: Compare annual leave in Finland and Hong Kong.
references.ground_truth: These are fictional local demo policies, not confirmation of real employment entitlements. Finland's accrual year is 1 April to 31 March. Each full qualifying month earns 2 arkipäivää if employment has lasted less than one year as at 31 March, or 2.5 arkipäivää if it has lasted at least one year. A full month follows the 14-day or 35-hour rule; certain sickness, family-leave and layoff absences count as work. Summer leave is mainly 2 May to 30 September. Employee preferences are heard before dates are confirmed, normally one month ahead or at least two weeks ahead. Leave exceeding 18 arkipäivää may be saved by agreement. Monthly salary continues during annual leave; unused leave is compensated on termination. Holiday bonus follows the collective agreement. Incapacity at the start of or during leave must be reported promptly with reliable evidence. Hong Kong provides 14 paid working days per calendar year, no less than the statutory entitlement, with joining/leaving-year proration. Up to five company annual-leave days can carry over and must be used by the end of March. Planned leave of two days or more is normally requested seven days ahead; exactly two days is included. Managers respond within two working days and give business reasons for refusal. Statutory annual-leave arrangements and unused-leave payment follow the Employment Ordinance. Do not equate Finnish arkipäivää with Hong Kong working days without an established conversion.

samples.reason: The answer says planned leave of more than two days, excluding exactly two days contrary to HR-HK-003 page 3. This is a critical source-fidelity discrepancy for this sanity check, not an assertion that every other metric must fail.
The recorded answer preserves the local entitlements, counting units, inclusive two-day threshold, carryover limits and local precedence.

references.query: What is the maternity leave policy in Hong Kong?
references.ground_truth: The supplied Hong Kong document is explicitly a fictional demo, not a confirmed employment entitlement. Maternity leave is no shorter than the statutory duration; the company's demonstration arrangement is 16 weeks at full pay. Maternity leave is handled under the Employment Ordinance, and statutory entitlements and eligibility follow the Labour Department's published requirements. Planned leave lasting two days or more is normally requested seven days in advance, including a request lasting exactly two days. Managers respond within two working days and provide business reasons for refusal. Maternity leave and other protected absences must not be improperly refused because of staffing arrangements. The supplied policy information does not establish detailed eligibility criteria, required supporting documents or when maternity leave must begin; do not invent those details or replace the fictional arrangement with external statutory figures.

samples.reason: The main 16-week demonstration arrangement is correctly labeled, but the extra application guidance incorrectly changes two days or more into more than two days.
The recorded answer preserves the fictional scope, 16 weeks at full pay, inclusive planned-leave threshold, response time and uncertainty about unspecified eligibility details.

references.query: When is salary paid in Finland and what benefits are included?
references.ground_truth: These Finland policies are fictional demos, not real employment-policy guarantees. Monthly salary is paid on the last banking day of the month. Listed benefits are lunch at EUR 13 per working day, sports and culture at EUR 400 per year, commuting up to EUR 800 per year, a bicycle leasing programme under applicable tax rules, and a one-time EUR 300 reimbursement for approved home-office ergonomics. Statutory TyEL pension, unemployment, accident and group-life insurance are arranged according to law. Preventive occupational healthcare covers employees from their first working day, with additional GP-level medical care, early support and return-to-work support. The demo holiday bonus is 50 percent of holiday pay, paid with June's salary, based on the applicable collective agreement or employment contract rather than the Annual Holidays Act. The payslip shows salary components, benefits in kind, tax withholding and other deductions; errors are corrected promptly and substantial underpayments in a separate run. The available Finland leave policy supplies the local leave benefits: annual leave accrues over 1 April to 31 March at 2 arkipäivää per full qualifying month if employment has lasted less than one year as at 31 March, or 2.5 arkipäivää if it has lasted at least one year. A full month follows the 14-day or 35-hour rule. Monthly salary continues during annual leave, and unused leave is compensated on termination. Each parent receives a demo top-up to a total of 16 weeks at full pay. Sick pay follows law and the collective agreement; self-certified absence is allowed for up to three consecutive days, with an occupational-health certificate for longer absence. Childcare leave is possible until the child turns three; temporary care leave for a suddenly ill child under ten is up to four working days at a time. Carer's leave is up to five working days per year subject to legal conditions. Other local benefits include five paid working days for bereavement, one paid working day for the employee's wedding, two paid days per year for volunteering, statutory unpaid study leave, and reservist-refresher pay under the collective agreement. Do not substitute the Global 22-working-day annual-leave baseline or unspecified Global parent leave for these available Finland terms, even if the payroll passages alone omit them. Global may supplement only topics for which no applicable country policy is available. Applicable law, collective agreements and the employment contract take precedence over the demo.
